advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Clear DEFER_FILE on the backoff-active early-exit path (autodeploy.sh:233) so a stale deferral episode cannot survive into a later deploy and prematurely trip the bound.
evidence: Line 230-234: `if [ "$bo_sha" = "$TARGET" ] && [ "$(now)" -lt "${bo_next:-0}" ]; then log "backoff active..."; exit 0; fi` — this early exit does NOT `rm -f "$DEFER_FILE"`.
DEFER_FILE is cleared only at line 228 (up-to-date), line 328 (drain-gate pass-through), and line 429 (success footer).

The stale-episode hazard is explicitly acknowledged and tested elsewhere: tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py `test_a_stale_deferral_episode_cannot_kill_a_later_review` ('the next busy tick inherits a spent bound and interrupts a review immediately'), but that test only exercises the up-to-date and idle-deploy clear paths, not the backoff-active skip.

Scenario: episode opens for TARGET=Y (busy), then main reverts to SHA X still within its backoff window; the tick exits at line 233 with DEFER_FILE retaining Y's episode timestamp; when backoff expires and the bot is busy again, `waited = now - (old defer_since)` can already exceed DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX and a review is killed on the first tick instead of being deferred.
advisory.finding: The deferral-episode marker file (DEFER_FILE) is not cleared on the backoff-active early-exit path (autodeploy.sh:233), so a stale episode timestamp can survive and later trip the bound to interrupt a review on its first busy tick.
scenarios: A deploy of SHA X fails and enters backoff; a newer SHA Y lands and the bot is busy (episode opens); main is then reverted to X while X is still in its backoff window and the bot is still busy.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `rm -f "$DEFER_FILE"` to the backoff-active branch before `exit 0` at line 233 (a backoff-active tick means no deploy is proceeding this cycle, so any open episode is not the one being deferred).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the app.py source-grep in test_health_exposes_in_flight_without_needing_the_reviewbot_extra with a fastapi-free behavioral assertion on the /health handler's return value (e.g. asyncio.run(app.health()) → assert result['in_flight'] is an int).
evidence: app.py is executable source under test (src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:210 @app.get("/health"))

The behavioral endpoint test is fastapi-gated: tests/unit/test_review_bot_in_flight.py:113 `pytest.importorskip("fastapi")`; the reviewbot extra is absent in the default `make test` tier (tests/unit/test_llm_capabilities.py:17 'the CI env running make test does not have it')
Litmus (Rule 4): renaming _voter.in_flight_reviews or building the dict via `{**base, ...}` would break this test with no observable-behavior change — a change-detector, not a behavior-verifier
advisory.finding: test_health_exposes_in_flight_without_needing_the_reviewbot_extra asserts by grepping the source-under-test (app.py) for the exact implementation expression '"in_flight": _voter.in_flight_reviews()' rather than the observable /health response. This is a source-grepping change-detector: a behavior-preserving refactor of how the handler constructs its response dict breaks the test while /health still returns a correct in_flight field. It is the ONLY in_flight coverage in the default CI tier (the behavioral endpoint test is importorskip('fastapi')-gated and skipped), so the field's actual runtime value is never behaviorally verified where it gates.
scenarios: A future refactor builds the /health payload differently (helper, dict-merge, key rename) while preserving the returned field — the grep breaks even though behavior is correct
The field is silently removed but a differently-spelled equivalent produces it — grep passes/fails on text, not on the parsed field
advisory.suggested_fix: Call the handler coroutine directly (it needs no fastapi): `import asyncio; from rebar.review_bot.app import health; monkeypatch.setattr(voter,'in_flight_reviews',lambda:2); body=asyncio.run(health()); assert body['in_flight']==2 and isinstance(body['in_flight'],int) and not isinstance(body['in_flight'],bool) and body['status']=='ok'`. This verifies observable output in the default tier and survives refactors.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral test that runs the reconciler over a stubbed review (monkeypatching gerrit fetch) and asserts voter.in_flight_reviews() is non-zero WHILE the reconcile review executes, instead of grepping reconcile.py source.
evidence: reconcile.py is executable source under test (src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py:223 `_voter.review_and_vote(ev, config=cfg, gerrit=gc, dedup=store)`)

No test drives a reconcile pass to observe voter.in_flight_reviews() > 0 during a backfill review — the claimed 'coverage that matters most' (module docstring lines 9-13) is asserted only by text-grep
Litmus (Rule 4): renaming the private _review_and_vote helper, or reconcile calling a new counted entry point with a different name, would break this test with identical observable behavior
advisory.finding: test_the_reconciler_path_is_counted_too asserts by grepping the source-under-test (reconcile.py) for the absence of the substring '_review_and_vote' and presence of 'review_and_vote', rather than exercising a reconcile review and observing in_flight_reviews() increment. This is a source-grepping change-detector: a behavior-preserving change (reconciler routed through a renamed-but-still-counted wrapper, or the private helper renamed) breaks it without any behavior change, and the actual contract (a reconciler review IS counted in-flight) is never executed.
scenarios: Reconcile is refactored to call a new counted wrapper; the grep for '_review_and_vote' absence fails despite correct counting
The private helper _review_and_vote is renamed for clarity; unrelated test breakage
A regression where reconcile bypasses counting via some other path the grep does not model passes undetected
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch voter._review_and_vote to record voter.in_flight_reviews() (mirroring test_review_and_vote_is_counted_while_it_runs), then drive one reconcile candidate through the reconcile loop's review_and_vote call and assert the recorded count == 1 — an observable, refactor-safe verification of the reconciler path being counted.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend capture_bot_logs' token redaction to cover AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED and AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT (not just AUTODEPLOY_ERROR), so captured bot-log text can never inflate the new journal-counted metrics.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:144-147 marker() header: 'a token is an alarm contract — never reuse one for a different meaning, and never let captured text carry one (see capture_bot_logs' redaction).'
autodeploy.sh:186 only redacts one token: `log "bot-unhealthy diagnostics ... ${out//AUTODEPLOY_ERROR/AUTODEPLOY_ERR<redacted>}"`

observability.sh:216-219 counts the two new tokens from the same unit journal: `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED ...` and `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT ...`
observability.sh:204 the grep is over the whole unit journal (`journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy.service ... | grep -cE "$token"`), which includes capture_bot_logs' log() output
dropped.finding: capture_bot_logs redacts only the AUTODEPLOY_ERROR token, but this change adds two new journal-counted tokens (AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED, AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT) that observability.sh counts from the same unit journal — so a review-bot log tail containing either literal string, echoed unredacted by capture_bot_logs, would inflate the deploy_deferrals / review_interrupts CloudWatch metrics (the latter drives a paging alarm).
scenarios: A review-bot whose stderr/log tail happens to print the string AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT (e.g. echoing its own deploy markers, test fixtures, or an operator message) during a failed health check — capture_bot_logs writes it into the journal and the interrupts metric spuriously increments, paging on a review that was never killed.
dropped.suggested_fix: In capture_bot_logs (line 186), redact all countable tokens, e.g. after building $out: `for t in AUTODEPLOY_ERROR AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT; do out="${out//$t/${t}<redacted>}"; done` before passing to log().
